jobs.title: Assistant Professor - Arthropod Biodiversity - Department of Environmental Science, Policy, and Management
jobs.description:
**Position overview Position title:** Assistant Professor Salary range: The current salary range for this position is $84,100–$132,900 (9\-month academic year salary), however, off\-scale salary and other components of pay, which would yield compensation that is higher than this range, are offered to meet competitive conditions. Anticipated start: July 1, 2027 Application Window
  
**Open date:** August 24, 2026
  
**Next review date:** Friday, Oct 9, 2026 at 11:59pm (Pacific Time)
  
Apply by this date to ensure full consideration by the committee.
  
**Final date:** Friday, Oct 9, 2026 at 11:59pm (Pacific Time)
  
Applications will continue to be accepted until this date. Position description
  
The Department of Environmental Science, Policy, and Management (ESPM) at the University of California, Berkeley (UCB) invites applications for a tenure\-track Assistant Professor nine\-month faculty position in the area of Arthropod Biodiversity.
  
Biodiversity lies at the heart of all ecosystems, from the smallest microbiomes to the global expanses of continents, oceans, and the atmosphere. It holds intrinsic value across many dimensions, encompassing species, genes, functions, processes, and cultures, while also providing tangible benefits such as food, medicine, and other natural products. Biodiversity underpins essential ecosystem services, including clean air, water, and soil, and contributes profoundly to human health, cultural identity, and psychological well\-being. Arthropods, which E.O. Wilson famously described as “the little things that run the world,” are the majority of Earth's macrobiota and have recently faced threats from multiple stressors, including climate change, habitat loss and degradation, and cumulative use of agricultural chemicals.
  
Loss of biodiversity, both locally (α\-diversity) and among locations (β\-diversity) is occurring at a rate exceeding our current efforts to discover, document, and understand the species with which we share our planet. These patterns are particularly true for arthropods, with insects showing global declines in populations across multiple orders (sometimes referred to as “insect apocalypse”). At the species level, arthropods now represent 70\-80% of the documented loss of biodiversity. At the same time, many other arthropods are becoming increasingly problematic as invasive species, pests of agriculture and forests, and vectors of plant and animal pathogens. Expertise is needed in understanding drivers of arthropod biodiversity change, including understanding processes leading to resilient populations, communities, and ecosystems.
  
ESPM is a multidisciplinary community of scholars from across the sciences and humanities who conduct research, teaching, and outreach to advance scientific understanding and develop solutions for the world's pressing environmental problems. ESPM is home to a top\-ranked Ph.D. program in environmental science, environmental studies, and ecological/evolutionary biology. Our undergraduate students have a choice of vibrant majors that span the disciplines in the department.
  
ESPM is committed to addressing the family needs of faculty, including dual career couples and single parents. We are also interested in candidates who have had non\-traditional career paths, who have taken time off for family reasons, or who have achieved excellence in careers outside academia. For information about potential relocation to Berkeley, or career needs of accompanying partners and spouses, please visit the Office for Faculty Equity and Welfare's website .
  
**Department :** https://ourenvironment.berkeley.edu/ Qualifications Basic qualifications (required at time of application)
  
Applicants for this position must hold a Ph.D. (or equivalent international degree) or be enrolled in a Ph.D. (or equivalent international degree) granting program at the time of application. Preferred qualifications
  
The successful applicant will develop an internationally recognized research and teaching program focusing on terrestrial arthropod biodiversity in studies of (but not limited to) ecology, arthropod data science, disease biology, community/ecosystem ecology, conservation biology, systematics, evolutionary biology, and biological interventions (including management, removals, biological control, bioremediation, restoration, climate\-adaptation). We encourage applicants whose research contributes to the design, management, and integrated understanding of biodiverse systems, using any of many approaches, including (but not limited to) field surveys, use and integration of natural history collections, ecological manipulations, genomics, AI, and computational biology.
  
The successful candidate will have a doctoral degree in a relevant field such as, but not limited to, biological disciplines (including ecology, evolutionary biology, conservation biology, systematics), environmental sciences, geography, entomology, or related fields. The successful candidate will demonstrate:
  
Expertise in any area of terrestrial (non\-marine) arthropod biodiversity research.
  
Organismal expertise (e.g., ecological, evolutionary, systematic, etc.) in a taxon or group of taxa in any habitat, including but not limited to terrestrial and freshwater ecosystems, including working landscapes.
  
The ability to establish an innovative research agenda in partnership with other disciplines.
  
An interest in participatory research with practitioners and communities and the translation of science into solutions via policy and/or partnerships with government agencies, NGOs, or business.
  
Strong research productivity, potential for external funding, and a commitment to excellence in teaching.
  
Commitment to supporting the success of all students with effective mentoring and innovative classroom pedagogy.
  
Willingness to engage in service and leadership activities within the University and their profession. Application Requirements Document requirement

jobs.title: Scientist I (Metals), Eurofins Drinking Water and Wastewater West, Pomona, CA
jobs.description:
**Company Description**  

Eurofins Scientific is a network of independent companies providing a unique range of analytical testing  

services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic, and labelling is accurate.


Eurofins is dedicated to delivering testing services that contribute to the health and safety of society and the planet, and to its corporate responsibility to protect the environment and ensure diversity, equity, and inclusion across the entire network of Eurofins companies.


With over 50 laboratories and more than 40 service centers nationwide, Eurofins Environment Testing provides full\-service environmental analysis across all 50 states. Our network supports public and private clients—including DoD, DOE, and municipalities—through robust logistics and continuous investment in people, technology, and infrastructure. We offer comprehensive testing for air, water, soil, sediment, tissue, and waste, covering a wide range of analytes including PFAS, metals, VOCs/SVOCs, dioxins/furans, radiochemicals, and more.

 **Job Description**  

 Eurofins Drinking Water and Wastewater West in Pomona, CA is the largest and most recognized water and beverage testing laboratory in the United States, providing water quality compliance and specialty testing to more than 500 municipal, State and Federal customers.


 Eurofins Drinking Water and Wastewater West has a Scientist I opening at our Pomona Laboratory in the Metals department. This is a full time position, 40 hrs/week.


Duties include:

* Routine sample preparation and analysis of water samples by various written EPA and Standard Methods procedures,
* Performing data process, data entry and written documentation
* Performing routine instrument maintenance.
* Preparation of reagents and standards.
* Other general laboratory related duties as assigned
* Will include regular late shift and/or weekend duties.

  

**Qualifications**  

* Minimum BS/BA degree in chemistry and /or other related science field; one to two years of laboratory experience.
* One to two years of ICP\-OES and ICP\-MS (EPA 200\.7/EPA 200\.8\) experience preferred.
* Must be available to work overtime including weekends.
* Excellent math and computer skills
* Excellent written and communication skills
* Excellent attention to details and good organization skills
* Ability to work well independently as well as in a team environmen

  

**Additional Information**  

This is a full time position Tuesday to Saturday 9 am to 6 pm with possibility of overtime.

**Pay Rate Range for this position is** **$22\.20 \- $25 (DOE).**


Candidates within a commutable distance to Pomona, CA are encouraged to apply.


Eurofins Environment Testing (USA) provides a compensation range for informational purposes, the actual base salary may vary based upon, but not limited to, relevant experience and skill set, base salary of internal peers, business sector, and geographic location.


As a Eurofins employee, you will become part of a company that has received national recognition as a great place to work. We offer excellent full\-time benefits including comprehensive medical coverage, life and disability insurance, 401(k) with company match, paid holidays, paid time off, and dental and vision options.

**To learn more about Eurofins, please explore our website www.eurofinsus.com**

**We support your development!** Do you feel you don’t match 100% of the requirements? Don’t hesitate to apply anyway! Eurofins companies are committed to supporting your career development.

**We embrace diversity!** Eurofins network of companies believe in strength and innovation through diversity, being an Equal Opportunity Employer. We prohibit discrimination against employees or applications based on gender identity and/or expression, race, nationality, age, religion, sexual orientation, disability, and everything else that makes employees of Eurofins companies unique.

**Sustainability matters to us!** At Eurofins, we believe sustainability is at the heart of everything we do. Guided by our vision to be the Global Leader in “Testing for Life,” our mission to contribute to a healthier and safer world, and our core values, we are building a strong foundation for Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives. Eurofins’ commitment to sustainability begins within our own companies through a shared responsibility to people and the planet. With climate change posing an imminent threat, Eurofins and its many companies recognize their duty to proactively reduce or offset the environmental impact of essential operations while also helping our clients do the same—serving as a true ESG Enabler.

**Find out more in our career page: https://careers.eurofins.com/**

 **Eurofins USA Environment Testing is a Disabled and Veteran Equal Employment Opportunity employer.**

jobs.title: Senior Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
Join a growing Queensland environmental team where you will influence major infrastructure, energy, water, defence and resource projects while shaping environmental outcomes for regional communities. We have several long\-term environmental programs in Central QLD and numerous opportunities for work across multiple sectors that will benefit from your environmental expertise.


CQG Consulting (CQG) has recently become part of Beca, one of Asia Pacific’s largest independent advisory, design and engineering consultancies. Together CQG and Beca are strengthening our environmental science, ecology, GIS, stakeholder engagement, planning and approvals capability across regional Queensland. Both CQG and Beca have built their businesses on trusted relationships, outcome\-focused advice and a strong understanding of their clients and the communities in which they work.


**The Opportunity**

We are looking for an experienced **Environmental Scientist** to lead our environmental monitoring programs. The role will see you design and manage monitoring programs, coordinate teams, interpret environmental data, assess compliance and prepare high\-quality scientific reports. Providing technical leadership across monitoring programs, with the opportunity to work on major infrastructure, energy, water, Defence and resource projects.


You will be responsible for the effective delivery of environmental monitoring programs, particularly surface water and groundwater monitoring, and assess the data for Environmental Authority compliance reporting.


While this is primarily a program management, technical and reporting role, you will need a strong practical understanding of environmental field sampling and equipment. You will occasionally undertake or oversee field activities, particularly where technical expertise, troubleshooting or quality assurance is required.


You will also play an important role in ensuring junior staff and field teams are applying appropriate sampling techniques and quality assurance procedures.


You will be a key part of a tight\-knit team of trusted advisors, scientists and environmental specialists, committed to meeting the environmental goals for projects of all sizes. As a team we strive to provide sustainable, culturally sensitive and pragmatic solutions that contribute to making every day better. We also like to have fun along the way, so a good sense of humour will hold you in good stead.


**About You**

You will ideally have a degree or diploma in chemistry, environmental science, environmental engineering, earth science, natural resources or a related discipline, as well as a demonstrated experience managing environmental monitoring programs. Strong practical knowledge and demonstrated experience of surface water, groundwater sampling techniques, will enable you to supervise, mentoring or training junior environmental staff.


You will also have experience in assessing environmental data against Queensland Environmental Authority conditions and regulatory requirements a strong understanding of sampling QA/QC, laboratory analysis and data quality requirements.


Knowledge of the Queensland Environmental Protection Act 1994 and relevant environmental legislation, guidelines and standards is a must, and you will have experience using Monitor Pro or similar environmental data management and reporting software, or the demonstrated ability to quickly learn new systems.


Due to the nature of the work you will enjoy the opportunity to undertake occasional regional and remote travel when required.


**Ready to make the move? / Apply now**

If you want to make every day better, apply online today! If you have any questions, you can find out more about our people and projects by visiting cqgroup.com.au and www.beca.com


*By applying for this role, you consent to authorised hiring managers at Beca and CQG accessing and processing your application and personal information for recruitment purposes.*

*If you are successful in your application for this role you will be employed by CQG, a Beca company.*
